title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：pepper　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pepper 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the cook ① added the pepper that no guest in the canteen would have measured, and he said the adding was the whole of the day. The ② pepper, meaning the spice itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed unmeasured in the book; pepper, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ spoonful of pepper in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ pepper at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Pepper, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the cook said the measuring is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the pepper was the whole of the matter, meaning the heat and not the spice. The ⑥ pepper, meaning the heat and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; pepper, he said, is either something you add or the only word that means both spice and a heat. He said the heat is the part they remember.

By 1983 the ⑦ pepper had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ pepper of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of measuring; pepper, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ pepper I remember is the pepper measured in the menu, which closed in 1985 and is still measured as the quietest in the canteen. ⑩ Pepper, my mother said in 1987, is the only thing that improves by being measured; all pepper, she said, is a heat that has agreed to look like spice. She said the heat was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 胡椒；辣椒（指食堂里每一勺旁边的那一勺）
B. n. 胡椒；辣椒（指那撮胡椒本身，与小小的碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：add the pepper 撒这一撮胡椒
D. n. 胡椒；辣椒（指留给孩子们分着吃的那一份）
E. n. 胡椒之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的胡椒之事）
F. n. 胡椒；辣椒（指菜单里写到、被测量的那一撮）
G. n. 胡椒、辛辣（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 辛辣（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: added the pepper that no guest in the canteen would have measured
The pepper, meaning the spice itself and not the bowl
Every spoonful of pepper in that canteen
the pepper at the far table
the pepper was the whole of the matter
the pepper had become a line in a menu
The pepper of the whole thing

answers.why: add the pepper 意为“撒这一撮胡椒”，1978 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位客人肯测量的一撮胡椒做了一遍。
pepper 意为“胡椒；辣椒”，指那撮胡椒本身而不是小小的碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被测量。
pepper 意为“胡椒；辣椒”，指食堂里每一勺旁边的那一勺，每一勺旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
pepper 意为“胡椒；辣椒”，指最远那张桌角的留给孩子们分着吃的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
pepper 意为“胡椒、辛辣”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这撮辛辣就是那件事的全部。
pepper 意为“辛辣”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那撮胡椒，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
pepper 意为“胡椒；辣椒”，指菜单里写到、被测量的那一撮，到 1983 年这一撮成了菜单里的一行。
pepper 意为“胡椒之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的胡椒之事是一处食堂和三个日子的测量。
pepper 意为“胡椒；辣椒”，我记得的是菜单里测量过的那一撮，1985 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一撮。
pepper 为抽象总称，母亲 1987 年说，胡椒是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的胡椒。
